selection: All eight regularly scheduled 2025 FOMC decisions in the August 9, 2024 calendar. One correlated policy-year cluster. Retrospectively selected before these model calls; operator knows outcomes.
resolution_policy: YES if the original policy statement released at the specified scheduled meeting announces a lower federal-funds target upper bound than immediately before that meeting. NO if unchanged or increased. This concerns the action AT that meeting, not a cumulative cut by that date. Unscheduled actions, subsequent meetings and later interpretations do not settle this question. An unavailable or cancelled original statement is unresolved, not NO.
evidence_policy: Use only supplied factual evidence plus explicitly labeled judgmental probabilistic assumptions. No retrieval, tools, prior answers or known later outcomes. The event is future relative to the registered issue date.

cases.question: Will the FOMC lower the upper bound of its federal-funds target range at its scheduled decision on 2025-01-29, relative to the target immediately before that meeting?
cases.packet:
Evidence available before the forecast issue date 2025-01-15; this is a deliberately sparse supplied packet, not all information then available.
Federal Reserve statement published 2024-12-18: economic activity was expanding at a solid pace; labor market conditions had generally eased since earlier in the year; unemployment had moved up but remained low; inflation had progressed toward 2% but remained somewhat elevated. Risks to employment and inflation goals were roughly in balance. The FOMC cut the target range by 0.25 percentage point to 4.25–4.50%. Future adjustments would depend on incoming data, the outlook and risks. One voter preferred no change. Source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20241218a.htm
December 18, 2024 Summary of Economic Projections: median projected end-2025 federal-funds midpoint 3.9% (rounded), versus current midpoint 4.375%; projected 2025 real GDP growth 2.1%, Q4 unemployment 4.3%, Q4-to-Q4 PCE inflation 2.5%, core PCE inflation 2.5%. These are conditional participant projections, not observations or a promised meeting-by-meeting policy path. Source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcprojtabl20241218.htm
The calendar announced on 2024-08-09 lists eight 2025 scheduled decisions: January 29, March 19, May 7, June 18, July 30, September 17, October 29 and December 10. Source: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20240809a.htm
No 2025 decision outcomes or later observations are supplied. Estimate the probability for the specified meeting from this issue date; do not condition on unobserved earlier 2025 decisions. Label any judgmental assumptions.
